newsitem.title: USA: Technician sees CRB, T-bond yield down to yearend.
newsitem.headline: Technician sees CRB, T-bond yield down to yearend.

text.p: A drop last week in the Commodity Research Bureau (CRB) index and in U.S. Treasury bond yields sets the stage for continued declines into yearend, a technical market analyst said.

John Murphy, a financial television analyst who also heads his own consulting firm, JJM Technical Advisors, told investment advisors Tuesday at the Society of Asset Allocators and Fund Timers conference here that two technical signals last week point to a continued move.
Last Thursday, U.S. Treasury bond yields broke below the 40-week moving average for the first time since April.
The CRB index of 17 commodities fell to the lowest price for the year, both important signals, Murphy said.
"I don't think it's any coincidence that the exact same week that commodities broke down, bond yields broke down," he said.
Murphy pegged a downside target of 230.00 in the CRB index and saw potential for a drop in T-bond yield to 6.50 percent, possibly 6.25 percent.
"There may be a little window of opportunity" for the near term trend to continue, Murphy said.
